item.title: Ajax, ING and Ace & Tate hit by data breach
item.description:
Ajax, ING and Ace & Tate hit by data breach

August 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Football club Ajax, bank ING and eyewear chain Ace & Tate have been caught up in the data breach at logistics firm CEVA Logistics, which came to light this week when Bol and De Bijenkorf warned customers their details may have been exposed.

CEVA handles deliveries for the companies and had access to the customer data needed to fulfil orders. The firm says it cannot rule out that personal details were leaked, although the companies affected say no payment details, usernames or passwords were taken.

Whether addresses, email addresses or phone numbers were exposed remains unclear.

At ING, the breach affects customers who ordered physical products through the bank’s rewards points scheme.

Ajax has advised supporters to be extra alert to phishing messages in the coming weeks. The club and Ace & Tate have both reported the breach to privacy watchdog AP, as Bol did earlier this week.

Ace & Tate has warned customers that current orders may be delayed, although online ordering is still running. CEVA said it would respond to the breach at a later stage.

item.title: Actor Peter Faber, star of Dutch cinema’s golden age, dies at 82
item.description:
Actor Peter Faber, star of Dutch cinema’s golden age, dies at 82

August 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Peter Faber, one of the best-known faces of Dutch film and theatre for half a century, has died at the age of 82.

Faber was admitted to hospital in early July with breathing difficulties related to untreatable heart problems, his family told news agency ANP.

He broke through in the 1970s, widely regarded as the golden age of Dutch cinema, with roles in Keetje Tippel and Paul Verhoeven’s wartime classic Soldaat van Oranje – the film that later spawned the long-running musical which closed last month after 16 years.

He also took the title role in the 1976 film of Max Havelaar, Multatuli’s classic novel about Dutch colonial rule, and appeared alongside Sean Connery and Anthony Hopkins in Richard Attenborough’s A Bridge Too Far.

Faber began his career as a co-founder of Het Werkteater, an Amsterdam collective set up in the early 1970s to shake up Dutch theatre with performances about ordinary people and recognisable emotions. He won the Louis d’Or, the top Dutch theatre prize for a male actor, twice.

He kept working into his eighties. His final film role came in 2023 in Sweet Dreams, the Dutch entry for the 2024 Oscars, in which he appeared alongside his son Jesse.

Faber often spoke about his difficult upbringing, part of which he spent living on the streets of Amsterdam as a teenager. In 2008 he set up the Peter Faber Foundation to help young people build confidence, and to “make the switch from destructive to creative energy”. Its motto is “I can do it, I want it, I’m doing it. Now!”

A public memorial service will be held at Het Zonnehuis in Amsterdam-Noord on Monday between 10am and midday.

item.title: Cabinet rules out compensation for drought-hit businesses
item.description:
Cabinet rules out compensation for drought-hit businesses

August 7, 2026 Lauren Comiteau

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Despite the country’s continuing water shortage, entrepreneurs feeling the squeeze won’t be receiving any help from the government any time soon.

“There are arrangements in place for the event of a natural disaster, such as the flooding in Limburg in 2021, but we are not there yet,” infrastructure and water management minister Vincent Karremans said while visiting Nijmegen on Thursday.

“We don’t have the money in the account either. We can’t help it that it isn’t raining.”

Maarten Ouboter, a technician for the Amstel, Gooi and Vecht water authority, told DutchNews: “The question is: how much is a government – the public – responsible for the weather? The minister was clear: droughts can happen.”

Low water levels are hurting everyone from inland vessels that can’t sail down dwindling rivers to houseboat owners on the Rhine who have effectively been marooned. Several locks have been closed, ferries have been cancelled and the economically important Twente Canal, reported broadcaster NOS, is also inaccessible.

And while Karremans estimates that the economic damage to businesses runs “into the tens, if not hundreds of millions of euros”, he views the water shortage as an “entrepreneurial risk, after all” – not a natural disaster.

A shortage but not a crisis 
For now, the country’s water level remains at 2 – a shortage but not yet a crisis. That could change if the drought continues for another few weeks. But the government maintains its priorities are preserving the country’s dikes and ensuring enough available drinking water, not propping up businesses.

“We are now at a point that the rivers flowing into our low-lying delta have never been so low in August,” said Ouboter, who focuses on the Amsterdam area. “We are comparable to 1947, but that was in November.”

Using a football analogy, he said the drought “in June was ‘second league’; in July it was ‘first league’; in August, it’s Champions League.”

Boosting water storage
Karremans said more water must be stored for the future, including in places like the IJsselmeer and the Volkerak-Zoommeer. The cabinet is currently working on the Freshwater Delta Plan to ensure rainwater captured in the spring, for example, can be used in drier months.

In Amsterdam, an innovative system of wadis – dry water ditches – catches rainwater that can be distributed later where needed and also absorbs extra rainwater to prevent flooding.

“The way we think about water has changed,” said Ton Hilhorst, the chief garden designer at Amsterdam’s Artis zoo. “Water was always seen as the enemy, but now we must keep it in the country, not pump it out.”

Weather forecasters are predicting another warm and largely cloudless weekend, with rain unlikely in the current week.

item.title: Philip Morris rebuked over AI campaign against EU tobacco rules
item.description:
Philip Morris rebuked over AI campaign against EU tobacco rules

August 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch advertising standards watchdog RCC has reprimanded tobacco behemoth Philip Morris for an AI-powered ad campaign that it says violated the country’s tobacco advertising ban.

As the EU prepares its biggest tobacco tightening rules in 15 years, the public was invited to share its views via comments.

But a recent investigation by broadcaster NOS and the journalism platform Pointer found that Philip Morris used AI to generate hundreds of fake “citizen” responses opposing tougher EU rules on vapes, which along with other cigarette alternatives like e-cigarettes and heated tobacco, now account for 40% of the company’s revenue.

Here’s how the campaign worked: Philip Morris put up yellow posters carrying QR codes in tobacco shops under the slogan “Your Voice Your Choice.” Scanning the code led to a tool that asked multiple-choice questions and then an option to write a first-person text, which users could then send to the Commission.

The investigation found that some 71% of responses from the Netherlands were written by AI, the second highest after Portugal.

The RCC had several problems with the campaign, including that the text generator was paid for and owned by Philip Morris. The company defended its actions by saying it contributed to the public debate.

“The fact that the statements are framed as a call for public consultation does not detract from their commercial character,” said the watchdog.

The written responses also portray alternative tobacco products positively, which the RCC says constitutes advertising and therefore violates the tobacco advertising ban.

Doctors

In June, a group of doctors and healthcare campaign groups made a formal complaint to the RCC, saying the “misleading” campaign used an AI tool to influence European decision-making on tobacco and nicotine products.

Lawyer Laura van Gijn, who represents the doctors, told NOS that violating the tobacco advertising ban is a criminal offence. “This decision is a clear signal to the tobacco industry that digital influence campaigns do not fall outside the scope of the advertising ban, even when packaged as citizen participation. This precedent is relevant for similar campaigns elsewhere in Europe.”

item.title: No more “shame lips”: Dutch dictionary adds new word for labia
item.description:
No more “shame lips”: Dutch dictionary adds new word for labia

August 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Women’s rights groups are applauding the latest addition to the definitive Dutch dictionary Dikke Van Dale of the word labia: vulvalippen, added alongside the word schaamlippen.

While both words mean labia, the old schaamlippen translates as “shame lips”, which the organisations say is stigmatising as compared to the more neutral “vulva lips”.

“We should just mention these parts in our education with children and young people,” artist Esther van der Valk told broadcaster NOS. “People now know that this is a normal word, and with that we can break the taboo.”

Van der Valk is a member of Dolle Mina, the women’s rights group that was founded in the Netherlands in 1969 and has been advocating for the inclusion of vulvalippen in the Dutch dictionary to counter stigmatisation. They’re joined by Schaamteloos, a more recent campaign seeking to change language and attitudes regarding female anatomy.

Body positive

While schaamlippen will remain in the dictionary, the addition of vulvalippen means the word gets official Dutch language status – proof, say the activists, that the normalisation of sexuality via language can be achieved if enough people want it.

Schaamlippen is not the only word where shame is embedded in its name. There’s schaamhaar – “shame hair” – which is the name for pubic hair, schaambeen (shame bone) for pubic bone and even schaamstreek (shame area) for pubic area.

But Schaamteloos says it had to start somewhere, so it picked schaamlippen. “Everyone has pubic hair, a pubic bone, and a pubic area,” says the group, but “only half of us have labia – or ‘shame lips’ … which adds to a disproportionately large amount of trouble due to the taboo on talking about this.”

While some doctors and even the media have taken to using vulvalippen, it’s not yet part of the everyday Dutch vernacular.

That may change when the new anatomically correct word is included in the Dikke van Dale. That’s expected to happen during its next online update, likely this Autumn.

item.title: Four arrested for death threat against Breda mayor
item.description:
Four arrested for death threat against Breda mayor

August 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police have arrested four men suspected of threatening to kill Breda mayor Paul Depla, after a photograph found on a football supporter’s phone revealed new evidence for a case that had stalled.

A banner bearing the words “Depla Dood” (Depla dead) was hung on the front of a café in the city’s Meidoornstraat on March 8, when NAC Breda played Feyenoord. Depla reported the threat to the police, but in May prosecutors said the case had halted because the suspects could not be linked to the banner.

A breakthrough came when several NAC supporters were arrested over rioting around the club’s match against Heerenveen on May 10 and their phones were seized, police said. On one of them, officers found a photograph of the banner in which four men could be identified.

The four – three from Breda, aged 16, 32 and 34, and a 24-year-old from Oosterhout – were arrested on Thursday and will be questioned. Threatening a public official carries a maximum prison sentence of four years.

It is unclear what prompted the threat, but broadcaster NOS reported it may have followed a warning from the city council to a different café, which had planned to host a pre-match party for the club’s hardcore supporters.

When the owners called the party off, the group gathered at the Meidoornstraat café instead, where the banner was hung.

Threats and intimidation against Dutch public officials are a growing concern. Some 45% of local and regional political office holders, including mayors, told a 2024 home affairs ministry survey they had faced aggression in the preceding year.

item.title: Warm, dry weekend ahead as drought shows no sign of ending
item.description:
Warm, dry weekend ahead as drought shows no sign of ending

August 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands is set for another warm and largely cloudless weekend, with barely a drop of rain likely for the coming week, according to forecasters.

Friday will be calm and dry with temperatures of 21 to 25°, with morning cloud in the north east giving way to sunshine. Saturday will be sunny and slightly warmer, at 25 to 28°, before temperatures climb to around 30° inland on Sunday.

A brief cooler spell will push maximums down to around 25° on Tuesday, but forecasters expect the warmth to return later in the week – without any significant rain.

The dry spell means no let-up for the ongoing drought, which has pushed the Rhine to record low levels and prompted water use restrictions in several regions.

item.title: Childcare benefits falling short for most parents: CBS
item.description:
Childcare benefits falling short for most parents: CBS

August 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Almost two-thirds of parents who claim childcare benefits pay more than the government’s maximum hourly rate, leaving them with hundreds of euros in costs the benefit does not cover, according to national statistics agency CBS.

Parents claiming the benefit spent an average of €10,510 on childcare in 2025, of which 68% was covered, up from 65% in 2024. The benefit was raised in both years as a step towards the government plan for near-free childcare.

But childcare providers are free to set their own fees, and the benefit only applies to costs up to a ceiling fixed by the government each year. In 2025, 63% of parents paid more than the maximum rate for at least one child.

On average, parents paid €3,340 towards childcare themselves last year – €2,860 in regular contributions, plus an extra €480 to cover fees above the official maximum.

The share of parents paying over the ceiling varies widely. In Nunspeet, Bloemendaal, Houten and Midden-Delfland, almost 90% pay more than the maximum rate, compared with just 8% on the island of Ameland. The proportion is highest in the provinces of Utrecht and Noord-Holland and lowest in Friesland and Groningen.

Households in the lowest income group paid an average of €1,190 towards childcare, or 11% of the total cost, while the highest earners paid €5,950, just over half the bill.

In total, 719,000 parents claimed the benefit last year for nearly 1.1 million children. More children attended nurseries and after-school clubs, while the number looked after by registered childminders (gastouders) fell by 10,000 to around 95,000.

The cabinet plans to make childcare almost free for working parents from 2029, covering 96% of costs regardless of income – a scheme that has been repeatedly delayed.

item.title: Kodai Sano joins PSV in biggest Eredivisie move of the summer
item.description:
Kodai Sano joins PSV in biggest Eredivisie move of the summer

August 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

PSV Eindhoven are in a race against the clock to complete the signing of NEC Nijmegen midfielder Kodai Sano before the first match of the Dutch league season after the clubs agreed a fee of €14.5 million.

The deal, a record sale for the Nijmegen club, left a bitter aftertaste after Sano pulled out of the squad for the midweek Champions League match against Olympiakos despite travelling to Greece.

Director of football Carlos Aalbers said the 22-year-old, who was instrumental in the club’s third-place finish last year, was sent home from the team hotel because “agreements were breached”.

“Sano didn’t want to play and we didn’t want a player in the team who didn’t want to play,” he said.

The champions could be set to offload striker Couhaib Driouech to Rangers before the end of the transfer window. Dutch media report that the two clubs have agreed a price of around €8 million for the 24-year-old Morocco international, but no formal bid has been tabled.

PSV are also believed to be close to completing the signing of Serbian international Filip Kostic, who spent two seasons at Groningen earlier in his career. The arrival of the 33-year-old has fuelled speculation that Croatian veteran Ivan Perisic is on his way out of Eindhoven, most likely to join Inter Milan.

Reserve goalkeeper Joël Drommel is leaving PSV after five years, returning to Twente, the club where he made his professional debut in 2015. “It feels like coming home,” said Drommel, who spent last season on loan at Sparta.

Tadic returns

Another Serbian veteran, former Ajax striker Dusan Tadic, is back in the Netherlands after joining NEC on a three-year contract. “The Netherlands is my second home,” said the 37-year-old, who has also played for Groningen and Twente.

Feyenoord look set to hang on to 20-year-old defender Givairo Read after turning down bids from AS Roma and Nottingham Forest.

Neither club was prepared to match the asking price of €25 million plus €4 million in bonuses for Read, whose current contract runs to 2029.

The Rotterdammers and PSV both want to sign former Feyenoord defender Lutsharel Geertruida from RB Leipzig, but neither club is willing to match the Bundesliga club’s €20 million asking price. Leipzig also say they are not interested in a loan deal.

Ajax loan signings

The biggest name to join Ajax so far under new head coach Míchel is goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen, who is moving from Barcelona on a season-long loan.

The 34-year-old, who won the Champions League and seven La Liga titles with the Catalan side, spent part of last season on loan at Girona, Míchel’s previous club. “When I first spoke with [Ajax’s director of football] Jordi Cruyff, I immediately felt it was the right option,” he said.

Another experienced German moving to Amsterdam is 30-year-old midfielder Julian Brandt, who arrives on a free transfer from Borussia Dortmund.

The Amsterdammers are believed to be in contact with Napoli about bringing Noa Lang back to the club if, as expected, Belgian striker Mika Godts leaves for Paris Saint-Germain before the end of the month. The clubs are understood to be negotiating a five-year deal, but PSG are haggling over Ajax’s €60 million price tag.

Torrents as cover

Ajax have also signed 19-year-old midfielder Jofre Torrents on loan from Barcelona as possible cover for Owen Wijndal, who is rumoured to be seeking a move out of Amsterdam. If Wijndal stays, Torrents is likely to turn out for the youth team in the Keuken Kampioen Divisie.

Midfielder Kian Fitz-Jim is definitely leaving after Ajax agreed to sell the 23-year-old, who spent part of last season on loan at Excelsior, to Torino.

Calvin Stengs is back at AZ Alkmaar after four years, after being released from his contract at Feyenoord, while Republic of Ireland striker Troy Parrott is said to be considering a move from Alkmaar to English Championship with West Ham United.

Elsewhere in the Eredivisie, Excelsior have signed 20-year-old striker Aymen Sliti on loan from city neighbours Feyenoord.

Swedes at Groningen

Groningen have signed 18-year-old Swedish midfielder Alvin Nordin from Helsingborgs on a four-year deal. Nordin played 28 first-teammatches for the Swedish club after making his debut at 16. Another Swede, defender Malcolm Jeng, is moving to the Euroborg on loan from Stade de Reims.

The northerners have also turned down a bid from AZ for striker Thom van Bergen. “We’ve made it clear Thom is not for sale,” managing director Frank van Mosselveld told RTV Noord.

Newly promoted Willem II have acquired 29-year-old midfielder Hidde ter Avest from English third-tier side Oxford United.

Telstar have strengthened their midfield with the signing of 20-year-old Harrie Kuster from Twente, 20-year-old Isiah Ahmed from Heerenveen and 23-year-old Gabi Caschili, who was released by Cambuur Leeuwarden a year ago after he was involved in a brawl during an amateur match.

item.title: Dutch rights group COC wins Pride Award for 80 years of work
item.description:
Dutch rights group COC wins Pride Award for 80 years of work

August 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch campaign group COC Nederland, the oldest surviving LGBTQI+ rights organisation in the world, has won the International Pride Award at the WorldPride Human Rights Conference in Amsterdam.

The awards, a joint initiative of the United Nations Development Programme and ILGA World, were presented to five “equality champions” at a ceremony in the Beurs van Berlage on Wednesday. Amsterdam is hosting WorldPride, the global LGBTQI+ event, for the first time this year.

The COC, founded in 1946, was recognised in particular for its support for people in countries where homosexuality is banned or even punishable by death, director Marie Ricardo, who accepted the prize, told broadcaster NOS.

“We support them with coaching, we help them think about how to bring about change in their own surroundings, and we support them with money,” she said.

Ricardo called the award “a recognition of the work we have been doing for 80 years, and the 40 years we have been supporting movements internationally”.

Other winners include South African deputy minister Mmapaseka Steve Letsike and Ugandan transgender pastor Aggie Dennett Harmon.
